title: `sqlparse.split` ends an anonymous `BEGIN ... END` block early at `END FOR`, `END IF` or `END CASE`
spec:
This is the sqlparse library (Python 3, no dependencies). Run the tests with `PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests`.

In an anonymous `BEGIN ... END;` block, nested control structures make the splitter close the block too early.

```python
import sqlparse
sql = """BEGIN
    SELECT 1;
    FOR R DO
        SELECT 1;
    END FOR;
END;"""
sqlparse.split(sql)
```
Expected: one statement.
Actual: `['BEGIN\n    SELECT 1;\n    FOR R DO\n        SELECT 1;\n    END FOR;', 'END;']`

A second case: a block containing `IF 1 THEN SELECT CASE WHEN 1 THEN 2 ELSE 3 END AS COUNT; ELSE SELECT 2; END IF;` comes back as four pieces instead of one; the inline `CASE ... END` expression closes the block.

The rule: inside a `BEGIN ... END` block, every nested `IF ... END IF`, `CASE ... END CASE` (procedural), inline `CASE ... END`, `FOR/WHILE ... DO/LOOP ... END FOR/END WHILE/END LOOP` and inner `BEGIN ... END` must be matched with its own closer, so only the block's own `END;` ends the statement. Statements after the block (e.g. a following `SELECT 3;`) must still be split off. `FOR UPDATE` / `FOR SHARE` in ordinary queries, inside or outside a block, are not loops.
acceptance: Both reported blocks split into exactly one statement
Blocks with sequential `FOR ... LOOP ... END LOOP` or `CASE ... END CASE` are one statement, and a statement after them is split off
`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE; SELECT 3;` still splits into two statements
Regression tests are added and the full test suite passes
